title: Comparison of henselian local inertia with inertia in a global separable closure
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $\Omega$, namely the elements satisfying a monic polynomial over $A$, and choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ above $\mathfrak m$. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$, $D=\{g\in G:g\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q\}$ and $I=\{g\in D:g|_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}=1\}$. Let $A^{\mathrm h}$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be compatible henselization and strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with residue fields $\kappa$ and a chosen separable closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. There are compatible embeddings $A\subseteq A^{\mathrm h}\subseteq A^{\mathrm{sh}}\subseteq B_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\Omega$ realizing the residue choice. Both henselizations are domains. With $K^{\mathrm h}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm h})$ and $K^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm{sh}})$, one has
$$D=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm h}}(\Omega),\qquad I=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega).$$
The field $\Omega$ is a separable closure of $K^{\mathrm h}$. Under this identification the residue homomorphism is the continuous surjection
$$D\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)$$
with kernel $I$. In particular the inertia kernel of the henselian local field $K^{\mathrm h}$, defined as the kernel of its absolute Galois group acting on the separable residue closure, maps to precisely $I\subseteq G$. All the group identifications use their Krull topologies. For any chosen compatible embedding $K^{\mathrm{sh}}\subseteq\Omega$ as above, the same conclusion identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)$ with that local inertia kernel.
